verdict.rationale: Codex documents automatic, description-driven skill activation. Agents start with each skill's name and description and load the full SKILL.md only when they decide to use it. The skill creator also asks when a skill should trigger, and a community user reports agents leverage skills when needed. However, guidance on engineering descriptions for accurate triggering is thin, and nothing hands-on shows the right skill reliably activates at the right moment. missing for 10: documented best practices for writing trigger-precise descriptions, evidence of activation accuracy or testing/evaluation of triggering, independent hands-on corroboration of reliable auto-activation.

support.subject: As a developer, installed skills trigger automatically from task context, with descriptions engineered so the agent activates the right skill at the right moment

citations.quote: ChatGPT and Codex start with each skill's name and description, then load the full `SKILL.md` instructions when they decide to use that skill.
The creator asks what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only or include scripts.
Because skills are a semi-special construct, agents are better at leveraging them when needed.
